title: Time Tracks
tagline: Scalping, intraday, swing and long term
principle: Scalping, intraday, swing and long-term investing
product: Brokerage, STT, short- and long-term capital gains tax
philosophy: Costs and stress rise as the horizon shrinks

lessons.title: Four speeds
lessons.subtitle: Seconds, a day, weeks or years
lessons.capability: Describe scalping, intraday, swing trading and long-term investing.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: I watch charts all day and trade every five minutes. That's investing, right?

steps.speaker: kip
lines: That's one speed, Dash. There are four.
The faster you go, the more you pay in costs and stress, and the more you're fighting random noise.

items.title: Scalping
items.text: Seconds to minutes. Dozens of trades a day for tiny moves. Costs and noise dominate.

items.title: Intraday
items.text: Opened and closed the same day, before the market shuts at 3:30 pm. No overnight risk, but costs every day.

items.title: Swing
items.text: Days to weeks. Held overnight, so surprise news can open a gap against you.

items.title: Long term
items.text: Years. Few trades, low costs, lower tax, and time for businesses to grow.

steps.question: A trade opened and closed on the same day is…

options.why: Yes. Indian stock markets close at 3:30 pm, and intraday positions are squared off by then.
Long term means years.
Swing trades are held overnight, for days or weeks.

steps.question: As the horizon gets shorter, what grows?

options.why: Right. More trades, more fees, and price moves that are mostly random.
Nothing is guaranteed at any speed.
Short-term gains are taxed more, not less.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: SEBI studies of intraday traders found about 7 in 10 lost money. Over long periods, broad Indian share indices have grown, with big dips along the way.
steps.deeper: Intraday trading in India uses leverage from the broker, which SEBI has steadily restricted with margin rules since 2020.

lessons.title: The toll on every trade
lessons.subtitle: Brokerage, taxes and spread
lessons.capability: Explain how trading costs compound against frequent traders.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Brokerage is only ₹20 a trade. That's nothing!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Add exchange charges, STT, GST, stamp duty and the spread between buy and sell prices.
It's small each time, but it comes off every single trade.

steps.title: How often do you trade?
steps.caption: Slide from a couple of trades a year to one every day.

steps.question: Why do costs hurt frequent traders so much?

options.text: They're paid on every trade, and add up
options.why: Yes. Costs compound against you, the way returns compound for you.

options.text: Brokers charge more to frequent traders
options.why: Costs per trade are similar; you just pay them far more often.
Try 250 trades a year on the slider.

steps.question: Shares held for over a year in India are taxed…

options.why: Right. Long-term capital gains on shares are taxed lower than short-term gains, with an exemption limit.
It's the other way round.
Gains above the exemption are taxed.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: On Indian shares, gains held under a year are taxed as short-term capital gains (20% in 2024 rules). Held over a year, long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year are taxed at 12.5%. Rules change, so check the current ones.
steps.deeper: STT (Securities Transaction Tax) is charged on every share trade in India, even losing ones. Your contract note lists every charge on each trade.

lessons.title: Timeframe Racer
lessons.subtitle: Same market, two speeds
lessons.capability: Compare frantic short-term trading with holding, on the same market.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Race you! I'll scalp, you hold. Same money, same market.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Deal. You tap as fast as you like. I'll tap once.

steps.title: Timeframe Racer
steps.caption: Round 1: scalp for 36 ticks. Round 2: hold for 5 years.

predict.question: Who usually ends up ahead?
predict.reveal: Over many tries, the holder usually wins: tiny moves are mostly noise, but costs are certain.

steps.question: Why does scalping usually lose to costs?

options.text: Tiny moves are mostly noise; costs are certain
options.why: Yes. You pay every time, but the gains are random.
They don't. They mostly wiggle.
Not true, though short-term gains are taxed more.

options.text: Time for businesses and returns to compound
options.why: Right. Growth needs years, not minutes.
Holding avoids needing good timing.
Holders ride falls too. They just don't have to sell in them.

steps.title: Card unlocked: Buy and Hold
steps.realLife: A low-cost index fund SIP, held for years, is buy-and-hold on autopilot. Fewer trades mean fewer costs, lower tax and calmer evenings.
steps.deeper: Studies of retail investors in many countries find that those who trade most earn the least, after costs.

lessons.title: Boss: The Long Track
lessons.subtitle: Patience as a superpower
lessons.capability: Choose a sensible time horizon and explain why it matters.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: I traded 400 times this year and ended up where I started. Minus fees.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Then let’s run all four tracks in one go: scalping, intraday, swing, then long term.
Watch which one keeps the most coins after fees.

steps.brief: Time Tracks! Four speeds in one run. Count the fees in the fast lanes, jump the overnight gaps, then enjoy the calm long-term road.

steps.title: Rematch
steps.caption: One more race: scalp, then hold.

steps.question: Which horizon fits money for retirement 40 years away?

options.why: Yes. Decades let compounding do the heavy lifting.
Minutes for a 40-year goal makes no sense.
Same-day trades are for short-term speculation.

steps.question: A swing trader holds over the weekend. What's the extra risk?

options.text: News can open a gap on Monday
options.why: Right. Prices can jump overnight before you can react.
Overnight news is the swing trader's big risk.
Very unlikely. The real risk is a price gap.

steps.title: World complete: Time Tracks
steps.realLife: You know the four speeds, what each costs, and why the slow track is where most long-term wealth is built.
